conceptPrimer.heading: SI Base Dimensions & Homogeneity Law
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: The seven SI base dimensions are $[M], [L], [T], [I], [\Theta], [N], [J]$. By dimensional homogeneity, only identical-dimension terms may be added or equated, and arguments of $\sin$, $e$, $\ln$ MUST be dimensionless. Micro-check: $\sin\omega t$ is legal because $\omega t$ is $[T^{-1}][T] = [T^0]$.

conceptPrimer.heading: High-Yield Dimensional Formulas
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Force $[MLT^{-2}]$; work and torque both $[ML^2T^{-2}]$ (same dimensions, different physics); viscosity $[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$; Planck's $h$ $[ML^2T^{-1}]$; and the trio $RC$, $L/R$, $\sqrt{LC}$ all reduce to $[T]$. Micro-check: $\frac{L}{R} = \frac{[ML^2T^{-2}I^{-2}]}{[ML^2T^{-3}I^{-2}]} = [T]$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Dimensionless vs Unitless
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Plane angle (rad) and solid angle (sr) carry SI units yet have dimension $[M^0L^0T^0]$ — dimensionless is NOT unitless. Conversely, torque and work share $[ML^2T^{-2}]$ while being different quantities. Micro-check: $[\varepsilon_0\mu_0]^{-1/2} = [LT^{-1}]$ — the speed of light.

conceptPrimer.heading: Error Propagation: Additive, Always
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Maximum errors add in sums AND differences: $\Delta(A \pm B) = \Delta A + \Delta B$. For $Z = \frac{A^pB^q}{C^r}$, fractional errors combine with POSITIVE exponent magnitudes: $\frac{\Delta Z}{Z} = |p|\frac{\Delta A}{A} + |q|\frac{\Delta B}{B} + |r|\frac{\Delta C}{C}$ — the denominator's $r$ still contributes $+|r|$ (errors never subtract). Micro-check: $Z = A/B$ with $2\%$ and $3\%$ errors: $\Delta Z/Z = 5\%$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Vernier & Screw-Gauge Least Counts
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Vernier: $\text{LC} = 1\,\text{MSD} - 1\,\text{VSD}$ (typically $0.1\,\text{mm}$). Screw gauge: $\text{LC} = \frac{\text{pitch}}{\text{circular divisions}}$ (e.g., $\frac{0.5\,\text{mm}}{50} = 0.01\,\text{mm}$). Corrected reading $=$ observed $-$ (signed zero error). Micro-check: pitch $1\,\text{mm}$ over $100$ divisions: LC $= 0.01\,\text{mm}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Significant Figures: the Trailing-Zero Rule
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Trailing zeros WITHOUT a decimal point are non-significant: $2500\,\text{m}$ has $2$ sig figs. Trailing zeros AFTER a decimal point are significant: $2.500\,\text{km}$ has $4$. Micro-check: $0.00320$ has $3$ sig figs (leading zeros never count; the trailing zero does).

memoryHooks: Homogeneity: add only what matches; functions eat dimensionless arguments.
Errors add in sums AND differences — never subtract.
Vernier: MSD minus VSD; screw: pitch over divisions.
Trailing zeros: the decimal point makes them significant.
commonMistakes: Subtracting errors in $Z = A - B$ or $Z = A/B$.
Counting trailing zeros of $2500$ as significant.
Confusing work and torque because dimensions match.
Forgetting the denominator exponent's magnitude in $\Delta Z/Z$.
Adding zero error instead of subtracting with sign.
Quoting radian as unitless rather than dimensionless.
Rushing the final unit conversion after a correct setup.
examChecklist: Check homogeneity of every option in dimension questions.
Recall force, work, viscosity, $h$, and the time-trio instantly.
Add all fractional errors with positive magnitudes.
Compute vernier/screw least counts from pitch/divisions.
Correct readings for signed zero error.
Count significant figures with the decimal-point rule.
